prompt:
Derive, from the definitions of velocity and acceleration, the constant-acceleration equation:
s = ut + 0.5 at^2
Show each step of your working clearly. [3 marks]
hints: Start from the definition of acceleration a = (v - u) / t and rearrange for v.
State the formula for average velocity during uniform acceleration.
Substitute v into the displacement equation s = v_avg t.
solution:
Step 1: From the definition of acceleration, a = (v - u) / t, so v = u + at [1 mark].
Step 2: For uniformly accelerated motion, the average velocity is v_avg = 0.5 (u + v) [1 mark].
Step 3: By definition of average velocity, displacement is s = v_avg t = 0.5 (u + v) t.
Substituting v = u + at: s = 0.5 [u + (u + at)] t = 0.5 (2u + at) t = ut + 0.5 at^2 [1 mark].
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Express final velocity from acceleration definition: a = (v - u)/t => v = u + at [1 mark].
Step 2: Express average velocity for constant acceleration: v_avg = (u + v)/2 [1 mark].
Step 3: Substitute v into s = v_avg x t: s = [(u + u + at)/2] t = ut + 0.5 at^2 [1 mark].
